1.contenido: 1. As the third millennium of the new era approaches, thoughts spontaneously go back to the words of the apostle Paul: "When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman" ([+[0]+]). Indeed, the fullness of time is identified with the mystery of the Incarnation of the Word, the Son consubstantial with the Father, and with the mystery of the Redemption of the world. Saint Paul emphasizes in this fragment that the Son of God was born of a woman, born under the Law, come into the world to rescue those who were under the Law, so that they could receive adoptive filiation. And he adds: «The proof that you are children is that God has sent into our hearts the Spirit of his Son who cries: Abba, Father! ». His conclusion is truly consoling: «So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, also an heir by the will of God » ( [+[1]+] ).

2.contenido: 2. Luke in his Gospel has given us a concise description of the circumstances surrounding the birth of Jesus: « It happened that in those days an edict went out from Caesar Augustus ordering that the whole world be registered ( [+[0]+] ). They all went to register, each one to their city. Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David, to register with Mary, his wife, who was pregnant. And it came to pass, while they were there, that her days of delivery were fulfilled, and she gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because they had no room in the lodging" ([+[1]+]).

3.contenido: 3. John, in the Prologue of his Gospel, summarizes in a single phrase the entire depth of the mystery of the Incarnation. He writes: "And the Word became flesh, and made his Dwelling among us, and we have contemplated his glory, glory that he receives from the Father as the only Son, full of grace and truth" ( [+[0]+] ). For John, in the conception and birth of Jesus the Incarnation of the eternal Word, consubstantial with the Father, takes place. The Evangelist refers to the Word that in the beginning was with God, through whom everything that exists was made; the Word in whom was life, life that was the light of men ( [+[1]+] ). Of the only begotten Son, God from God, the apostle Paul writes that he is "firstborn of all creation" ([+[2]+]). God creates the world through the Word. The Word is the eternal Wisdom, the Thought and the substantial Image of God, "the radiance of his glory and the imprint of his substance" ([+[3]+]). He, eternally begotten and eternally loved by the Father, as God from God and Light from Light, is the beginning and archetype of all things created by God in time.

4.contenido: 4. Christ, Redeemer of the world, is the only Mediator between God and men because there is no other name under heaven by which we can be saved ( [+[0]+] ). We read in the Letter to the Ephesians: "In Him we have through His blood redemption, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of His grace which He has lavished upon us in all wisdom and understanding ([+[1]+]) according to the benevolent plan which He purposed beforehand, to be accomplished in the fullness of time" ([+[2]+]). Christ, Son consubstantial with the Father, is therefore the One who reveals God's plan for all creation, and in particular for man. As the Second Vatican Council suggestively states, He "fully manifests man to himself and reveals to him the sublimity of his vocation." He shows him this vocation by revealing the mystery of the Father and his love. «Image of the invisible God», Christ is the perfect man who has restored to Adam's descendants the divine likeness, deformed by sin. In his human nature, free from all sin and assumed in the divine Person of the Word, the common nature of every human being is elevated to a very high dignity: «The Son of God with his incarnation has united himself in a certain way with every man. He worked with the hands of a man, he thought with the intelligence of a man, he acted with the will of a man, he loved with the heart of a man. Born of the Virgin Mary, he became truly one of us, similar in everything to us, except in sin.

5.contenido: 5. This "becoming one of us" of the Son of God occurred in the greatest humility, so it is not surprising that profane historiography, pending more clamorous events and more important figures, has dedicated only fleeting, although significant, allusions to him at the beginning. References to Christ are found, for example, in the Jewish Antiquities, a work written in Rome by the historian José Flavio between the years 93 and 94, and especially in the Annals of Tacitus, written between 115 and 120; In them, recounting the fire of Rome in 64, falsely imputed by Nero to the Christians, the historian makes explicit mention of Christ "executed by the work of the procurator Pontius Pilate under the empire of Tiberius." Also Suetonius in the biography of Emperor Claudius, written around 121, informs us about the expulsion of the Jews from Rome since "under the instigation of a certain Chrestus they caused frequent riots." Among interpreters, the conviction is widespread that this passage refers to Jesus Christ, who has become a cause of contention within Roman Hebraism. Also important, as proof of the rapid spread of Christianity, is the testimony of Pliny the Younger, governor of Bithynia, who tells the emperor Trajan, between 111 and 113, that a large number of people used to gather "on a set day, before dawn, to alternately sing a hymn to Christ as to a God."

6.contenido: 6. Jesus was born to the Chosen People, in fulfillment of the promise made to Abraham and constantly remembered by the prophets. These spoke in the name and place of God. In fact, the economy of the Old Testament is essentially ordered to prepare and announce the coming of Christ, Redeemer of the universe, and his messianic Kingdom. The books of the Old Alliance are thus permanent witnesses of an attentive divine pedagogy. In Christ this pedagogy reaches its goal: He does not limit himself to speaking "in the name of God" like the prophets, but it is God himself who speaks in his eternal Word made flesh. We find here the essential point by which Christianity differs from other religions, in which from the beginning man's search for God has been expressed. Christianity begins with the Incarnation of the Word. Here it is not only man who seeks God, but it is God who comes in Person to speak about Himself to man and to show him the path by which it is possible to reach Him. This is what the Prologue of the Gospel of John proclaims: "No one has ever seen God: the only Son, who was in the bosom of the Father, He has declared it" ([+[0]+]). The Incarnate Word is, therefore, the fulfillment of the desire present in all the religions of humanity: this fulfillment is the work of God and goes beyond all human expectations. It is a mystery of grace.

7.contenido: 7. In Jesus Christ God not only speaks to man, but seeks him. The Incarnation of the Son of God testifies that God seeks man. Jesus speaks of this search as the discovery of the lost sheep ( [+[0]+] ). It is a search that is born from the intimacy of God and has its climax in the Incarnation of the Word. If God goes in search of man, created in his image and likeness, he does so because he loves him eternally in the Word and in Christ he wants to elevate him to the dignity of adopted son. Therefore God seeks man, who is his particular property in a different way from each of the other creatures. It is the property of God through a choice of love: God seeks man moved by his Father's heart.

8.contenido: 8. The religion that springs from the mystery of the redeeming Incarnation is the religion of "remaining in the intimacy of God," of participating in his own life. Saint Paul speaks of this in the passage cited at the beginning: «God has sent into our hearts the Spirit of his Son who cries: Abba, Father! » ( [+[0]+] ). Man raises his voice in the likeness of Christ, who addressed God "with mighty cries and tears" ([+[1]+]), especially in Gethsemane and on the cross: man shouts to God as Christ shouted and thus bears witness to participating in his sonship through the work of the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit, which the Father sent in the name of the Son, makes man participate in the intimate life of God; It makes man also a son, in the likeness of Christ, and heir of those goods that constitute the Son's share ( [+[2]+] ). This is what the religion of "remaining in the intimate life of God" consists of, which begins with the Incarnation of the Son of God. The Holy Spirit, who plumbs the depths of God ( [+[3]+] ), introduces us, men, into these depths by virtue of the sacrifice of Christ.

9.contenido: 9. When Saint Paul speaks of the birth of the Son of God, he places it in "the fullness of time" ([+[0]+]). In reality, time has been fulfilled by the very fact that God, with the Incarnation, has entered into the history of man. Eternity has entered time: what "fulfillment" is greater than this? What other "compliance" would be possible? Someone has thought of certain arcane cosmic cycles, in which the history of the universe, and in particular of man, would constantly repeat itself. Man arises from the earth and returns to the earth ([+[1]+]): this is the data of immediate evidence. But in man there is an inalienable aspiration to live forever. How to think about your survival beyond death? Some have imagined various forms of reincarnation: depending on how one lived during the course of the previous existence, one would experience a new, nobler or more humble existence, until reaching full purification. This belief, deeply rooted in some Eastern religions, manifests among other things that man does not want to resign himself to an irrevocable death. He is convinced of his own essentially spiritual and immortal nature.

10.contenido: 10. In Christianity time is of fundamental importance. Within its dimension the world is created, within it the history of salvation develops, which has its culmination in the "fullness of time" of the Incarnation and its end in the glorious return of the Son of God at the end of time. In Jesus Christ, the incarnate Word, time becomes a dimension of God, who in himself is eternal. With the coming of Christ, the "last times" ([+[0]+]), the "last hour" ([+[1]+]) begin, the time of the Church begins, which will last until the Parousia.

11.contenido: 11. From this perspective, the use of jubilees, which began in the Old Testament and continues in the history of the Church, becomes understandable. Jesus of Nazareth went one day to the synagogue of his city and stood up to read ( [+[0]+] ). They gave him the volume of the prophet Isaiah, where he read the following passage: "The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is upon me, because Yahweh has anointed me." He has sent me to announce the good news to the poor, to bind up broken hearts; to proclaim liberation to captives, and freedom to prisoners; to proclaim the year of Yahweh's favor » ( [+[1]+] ).

12.contenido: 12. The words and works of Jesus thus constitute the fulfillment of the entire tradition of the jubilees of the Old Testament. It is known that the jubilee was a time dedicated in a particular way to God. It was celebrated every seven years, according to the Law of Moses: it was the "sabbatical year", during which the land was allowed to rest and the slaves were freed. The obligation to free slaves was regulated by detailed prescriptions contained in the Book of Exodus ([+[0]+]), Leviticus ([+[1]+]), Deuteronomy ([+[2]+]) and, practically, in all biblical legislation, which thus acquires this peculiar dimension. In the sabbatical year, in addition to the liberation of slaves, the Law provided for the remission of all debts, according to very precise regulations. All this was to be done in honor of God. What referred to the sabbatical year also applied to the "jubilee", which took place every fifty years. However, in the jubilee year the sabbatical practices were expanded and celebrated with greater solemnity. We read in Leviticus: « You will declare the fiftieth year holy, and you will proclaim liberation in the land for all its inhabitants. It will be a jubilee for you; “Everyone will recover his property, and everyone will return to his family” ( [+[3]+] ). One of the most significant consequences of the jubilee year was the "emancipation" of all the inhabitants in need of liberation. On this occasion each Israelite regained possession of the land of his parents, if he had eventually sold it or lost it by falling into slavery. The land could not be definitively deprived, since it belonged to God, nor could the Israelites remain forever in a situation of slavery, since God had "ransomed" them to himself as exclusive property by freeing them from slavery in Egypt.

13.contenido: 13. Although to a large extent the precepts of the Jubilee Year were no more than an ideal expectation - more a hope than a concrete realization, establishing on the other hand a prophetia futuri as a preannouncement of the true liberation that would have been achieved by the coming Messiah - on the basis of the legal regulations contained in them, a certain social doctrine has already been outlined, which was later developed more clearly from the New Testament. The jubilee year was to restore equality among all the children of Israel, opening new possibilities to families who had lost their property and even personal freedom. For its part, the jubilee year reminded the rich that the time had arrived when the Israelite slaves, once again equal to them, could claim their rights. In the time provided by the Law, a jubilee year was to be proclaimed, which came to the aid of all those in need. This required a just government. Justice, according to the Law of Israel, consisted above all in the protection of the weak, and the king must distinguish himself in this, as the Psalmist states: «For he will deliver the poor suppliant, the unfortunate and the one whom no one protects; He will take pity on the weak and the poor, he will save the soul of the poor » ( [+[0]+] ). The assumptions of these traditions were strictly theological, related above all to the theology of creation and that of divine Providence. In fact, it was a common conviction that only God, as Creator, had the "dominium altum", that is, lordship over everything created, and in particular over the earth ([+[1]+]). If God in his Providence had given the earth to men, this meant that he had given it to everyone. For this reason, the riches of creation should be considered a common good for all humanity. Whoever owned these goods as his property was in reality only an administrator, that is, someone in charge of acting on behalf of God, the sole owner in the full sense, it being God's will that the created goods serve everyone in a just way. The jubilee year was to serve in this way to reestablish this social justice. Thus, the social doctrine of the Church finds one of its roots in the tradition of the jubilee year, which has always had a place in ecclesial teaching and has been developed particularly in the last century, especially since the Encyclical Rerum Novarum.

14.contenido: 14. It is necessary to always emphasize what Isaiah expresses with the words: "proclaim a year of favor from the Lord." The Jubilee, for the Church, is truly this "year of grace", a year of forgiveness of sins and the penalties for sins, a year of reconciliation between adversaries, a year of multiple conversions and of sacramental and extra-sacramental penance. The tradition of the jubilee years is linked to the granting of indulgences in a more generous way than in other years. Along with the jubilees that remember the mystery of the Incarnation, the fulfillment of one hundred, fifty or twenty-five years, there are also those that commemorate the work of Redemption: the cross of Christ, his death on Golgotha ​​and his resurrection. The Church, in these circumstances, proclaims "a year of grace from the Lord" and strives so that all the faithful can enjoy this grace more widely. This is why jubilees are celebrated not only "in Urbe", but also "extra Urbem": traditionally this was done the year following the celebration "in Urbe".

15.contenido: 15. In the life of each person, jubilees normally refer to the day of birth, although the anniversaries of Baptism, Confirmation, First Communion, Priestly or Episcopal Ordination and the Sacrament of Marriage are also celebrated. Some of these anniversaries have their correspondence in the secular sphere, but Christians always attribute a religious character to them. In fact, in the Christian vision each jubilee - the 25th anniversary of the priesthood or marriage, called "silver", or the 50th, called "gold", or the 60th, "diamond" - constitutes a particular year of grace for the person who has received one of the listed sacraments. What we have said about individual jubilees can also be applied to communities or institutions. Thus, the centenary or millennium of the founding of a city or municipality is celebrated. And at the ecclesial level, the jubilees of the parishes or dioceses are celebrated. All these personal or community jubilees play an important and significant role in the lives of individuals and communities.

16.contenido: 16. The term "jubilee" expresses joy; not only internal joy, but a joy that is manifested externally, since the coming of God is also an external event, visible, audible and tangible, as Saint John reminds us ([+[0]+]). It is right, then, that every expression of joy for this coming has its external manifestation. This indicates that the Church rejoices in salvation, invites everyone to joy, and strives to create the conditions so that salvific energies can be communicated to each one. Therefore, 2000 will mark the date of the Great Jubilee.

17.contenido: 17. In the history of the Church each jubilee is prepared by divine Providence. This also applies to the Great Jubilee of the Year 2000. Convinced of this, today we look with a sense of gratitude and also responsibility at everything that has happened in the history of humanity since the birth of Christ, mainly the events between 1000 and 2000. In a very particular way we direct our gaze of faith to this century of ours, seeking in it that which bears witness not only to the history of man, but also to divine intervention in human vicissitudes.

18.contenido: 18. In this sense it can be affirmed that the Second Vatican Council constitutes a providential event, thanks to which the Church has begun the upcoming preparation of the Jubilee of the second millennium. It is a Council similar to the previous ones, although very different; a Council focused on the mystery of Christ and his Church, and at the same time open to the world. This openness has been the evangelical response to the recent evolution of the world with the disconcerting experiences of the 20th century, tormented by a first and a second world war, by the experience of concentration camps and by horrendous massacres. What happened shows above all that the world needs purification, it needs conversion.

19.contenido: 19. The Council, although it did not employ the severe tone of John the Baptist, when on the banks of the Jordan he exhorted penitence and conversion ([+[0]+]), has highlighted something of the ancient Prophet, showing with new vigor to the men of today Christ, the "Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" ([+[1]+]), the Redeemer of man, the Lord of history. In the conciliar Assembly the Church, wanting to be fully faithful to its Master, considered its own identity, discovering the depth of its mystery as the Body and Bride of Christ. Listening docilely to the Word of God, he confirmed the universal vocation to holiness; He ordered the reform of the liturgy, "source and culmination" of his life; It promoted the renewal of many aspects of its existence both at the universal level and at the local Church level; He was committed to promoting different Christian vocations: that of the laity and that of religious, the ministry of deacons, that of priests and that of Bishops; He rediscovered, in particular, episcopal collegiality, a privileged expression of the pastoral service carried out by the Bishops in communion with the Successor of Peter. On the basis of this profound renewal, the Council opened itself to Christians of other Confessions, to the followers of other religions, to all men of our time. In no other Council was the unity of Christians spoken so clearly, of dialogue with non-Christian religions, of the specific meaning of the Old Covenant and of Israel, of the dignity of personal conscience, of the principle of religious freedom, of the diverse cultural traditions within which the Church carries out its missionary mandate, of the media of social communication.

20.contenido: 20. The enormous wealth of content and the new tone, unknown before, of the conciliar presentation of these contents constitute almost an announcement of new times. The Council Fathers have spoken with the language of the Gospel, with the language of the Sermon on the Mount and the Beatitudes. The conciliar message presents God in his absolute lordship over all things, although also as guarantor of the authentic autonomy of temporal realities.

21.contenido: 21. The path of preparation for the 2000 event includes the series of Synods initiated after the Second Vatican Council: General Synods and continental, regional, national and diocesan Synods. The underlying theme is that of evangelization, better yet, that of the new evangelization, whose bases were established by the Apostolic Exhortation Evangelii nuntiandi of Paul VI, published in 1975 after the third General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops. These Synods are already part of the new evangelization in themselves: they are born from the conciliar vision of the Church, they open a wide space for the participation of the laity, defining their specific responsibility in the Church, and they are an expression of the strength that Christ has given to the entire People of God, making them part of his own messianic, prophetic, priestly and royal mission. The statements of the second chapter of the Const are very eloquent in this regard. dogm. Lumen gentium. The preparation for the Jubilee of the Year 2000 is thus carried out throughout the Church, at a universal and local level, animated by a new awareness of the saving mission received from Christ. This awareness is manifested with significant evidence in the post-synodal Exhortations dedicated to the mission of the laity, to the formation of priests, to catechesis, to the family, to the value of penance and reconciliation in the life of the Church and of humanity and, soon, to consecrated life.

22.contenido: 22. With a view to the Great Jubilee of the Year 2000, specific tasks and responsibilities await the ministry of the Bishop of Rome. All the Pontiffs of the century that is about to end have acted in some way along this line. With the program of renewing everything in Christ, Saint Pius X tried to prevent the tragic paths that the international situation at the beginning of the century was taking. The Church, faced with the consolidation in the contemporary world of tendencies opposed to peace and justice, was aware of the duty to act decisively to favor and defend such fundamental goods. The Pontiffs of the pre-conciliar period moved in this direction with great diligence, each one from his own situation: Benedict XV found himself faced with the tragedy of the First World War; Pius XI had to face the threats of totalitarian systems or systems that did not respect human freedom in Germany, Russia, Italy, Spain, and even before that in Mexico. Pius XII intervened against the greatest injustice of the Second World War, the utmost disregard for human dignity, and also gave luminous guidelines for the birth of a new world order after the fall of the preceding political systems.

23.contenido: 23. The current pontificate, from the first document, speaks explicitly of the Great Jubilee, inviting us to live the period of waiting as "a new advent." I have subsequently returned to this topic many other times, dwelling extensively on the Encyclical Dominum et vivificantem. In fact, the preparation for the Year 2000 is almost one of its hermeneutical keys. Certainly we do not want to induce a new millenarianism, as was done by some at the end of the first millennium; but rather the aim is to raise a particular sensitivity to everything that the Spirit says to the Church and the Churches ([+[0]+]), as well as to individuals through the charismas at the service of the entire community. It is intended to highlight what the Spirit suggests to different communities, from the smallest, such as the family, to the largest, such as nations and international organizations, without forgetting cultures, civilizations and healthy traditions. Humanity, despite appearances, continues to wait for the revelation of the children of God and lives from this hope, as one suffers the pains of childbirth, according to the image used with such force by Saint Paul in the Letter to the Romans ([+[1]+]).

24.contenido: 24. The Pope's pilgrimages have become an important element of the effort to implement the Second Vatican Council. Started by John XXIII, on the threshold of the inauguration of the Council, with a significant pilgrimage to Loreto and Assisi ( [+[0]+] ), they had a notable increase with Paul VI, who, after having gone first to the Holy Land ( [+[1]+] ), made nine other great apostolic journeys that brought him into direct contact with the populations of the different continents.

25.contenido: 25. In the preparation of the Year 2000, the particular Churches play their own role, which with their jubilees celebrate significant stages in the history of salvation of the various peoples. Among these local or regional jubilees, the millennium of the Baptism of Rus in 1988 and also the five hundred years of the beginning of the evangelization of the American continent have been of utmost importance ( [+[0]+] ). Along with these events of vast scope, although not of universal dimension, others that are no less significant must be remembered: for example, the millennium of the Baptism of Poland in 1966 and of Hungary in 1968, together with the six hundred years of the Baptism of Lithuania in 1987. In addition, the 1500th anniversary of the Baptism of Clovis king of the Franks will soon be celebrated ( [+[1]+] ), and the 1400th anniversary of the arrival of Saint Augustine to Canterbury ( [+[2]+] ), beginning of the evangelization of the Anglo-Saxon world.

26.contenido: 26. The Holy Years celebrated in the last period of this century are also placed in the perspective of the preparation for the Year 2000. The Holy Year that Pope Paul VI called in 1975 is still fresh in memory; Along the same lines, 1983 was later celebrated as the Year of Redemption. Perhaps an even greater echo was had by the Marian Year 198788, long awaited and deeply lived in the local Churches, and especially in the Marian shrines of the entire world. The Encyclical Redemptoris Mater, published at that time, evidenced the conciliar teaching on the presence of the Mother of God in the mystery of Christ and the Church: the Son of God became man two thousand years ago by the work of the Holy Spirit and was born of the Immaculate Virgin Mary. The Marian Year was like an anticipation of the Jubilee, including in itself much of what must be fully expressed in the Year 2000.

27.contenido: 27. It is difficult not to notice how the Marian Year closely preceded the events of 1989. These are events that are surprising for their magnitude and especially for their rapid development. The 1980s had followed one another with growing danger, in the wake of the "cold war"; The year 1989 brought with it a peaceful solution that has almost taken the form of an "organic" development. In its light we feel led to recognize an even prophetic meaning to the Encyclical Rerum Novarum: everything Pope Leo Furthermore, one could perceive how, in the plot of what happened, the invisible hand of Providence operated with maternal urgency: «Does a woman forget her suckling child...? » ( [+[0]+] ).

28.contenido: 28. Currently, following in the footsteps of the Marian Year and in a similar perspective, we are living the Year of the Family, whose content is closely linked to the mystery of the Incarnation and to the history of man itself. Therefore, we can hope that the Year of the Family, inaugurated in Nazareth, will become, like the Marian Year, a significant stage in the preparation of the Great Jubilee.

29.contenido: 29. In view of this vast panorama, the question arises: can a specific program of initiatives be drawn up for the immediate preparation of the Great Jubilee? In truth, what has been said above already presents some elements of such a program.

30.contenido: 30. A first indication, which emerged clearly from the consultation, is related to preparation times. The year 2000 is only a few years away: it has seemed appropriate to divide this period into two phases, reserving the actual preparatory phase for the last three years. It has been thought that a longer period would end up accumulating excessive content, attenuating spiritual tension.

31.contenido: 31. The first phase will therefore have a preparatory character: it should serve to revive in the Christian people the awareness of the value and meaning that the Jubilee of 2000 represents in human history. This, carrying with it the memory of the birth of Christ, is intrinsically marked by a Christological connotation.

32.contenido: 32. The Jubilee is always a time of particular grace, "a day blessed by the Lord": as such it has - I have already commented - a character of joy. The Jubilee of the Year 2000 wants to be a great prayer of praise and thanksgiving above all for the gift of the Incarnation of the Son of God and the Redemption accomplished by Him. In the jubilee year, Christians will place themselves with new amazement of faith in the face of the love of the Father, who has given his Son, "so that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have eternal life" ([+[0]+]). They will also raise with deep feeling their thanksgiving for the gift of the Church, founded by Christ as "sacrament or sign and instrument of intimate union with God and of the unity of the entire human race." His gratitude will finally extend to the fruits of holiness matured in the lives of so many men and women who in each generation and in each historical era have known how to accept without reservation the gift of Redemption.

33.contenido: 33. Thus it is right that, as the second Millennium of Christianity comes to an end, the Church assumes with a more vivid conscience the sin of its children, remembering all the circumstances in which, throughout history, they have distanced themselves from the spirit of Christ and his Gospel, offering to the world, instead of the testimony of a life inspired by the values of faith, the spectacle of ways of thinking and acting that were true forms of anti-witness and scandal.

34.contenido: 34. Among the sins that require a greater commitment to penance and conversion, those that have damaged the unity desired by God for his People must certainly be mentioned. Throughout the thousand years that are ending, even more than in the first millennium, the ecclesial communion, "sometimes not without the fault of men on both sides," has known painful lacerations that openly contradict the will of Christ and are a scandal for the world. Unfortunately, these sins of the past still make their weight felt and remain as temptations of the present. It is necessary to make amends, strongly invoking the forgiveness of Christ.

35.contenido: 35. Another painful chapter to which the children of the Church must return with a spirit open to repentance is constituted by the acquiescence manifested, especially in some centuries, with methods of intolerance and even violence in the service of the truth.

36.contenido: 36. A serious examination of conscience has been sponsored by numerous Cardinals and Bishops, especially for the Church of the present. At the gates of the new Millennium, Christians must humbly place themselves before the Lord to question themselves about the responsibilities that they also have in relation to the evils of our time. The current era, along with many lights, also presents many shadows.

37.contenido: 37. The Church of the first millennium was born from the blood of the martyrs: " Sanguis martyrum, semen christianorum ". The historical events linked to the figure of Constantine the Great would never have been able to guarantee a development of the Church such as that observed in the first millennium, if it had not been for that sowing of martyrs and for that heritage of holiness that characterized the first Christian generations. At the end of the second millennium, the Church has once again become the Church of martyrs. The persecutions of believers – priests, religious and lay people – have led to a great sowing of martyrs in various parts of the world. The testimony offered to Christ until the shedding of blood has become the common heritage of Catholics, Orthodox, Anglicans and Protestants, as Paul VI already revealed in the homily for the canonization of the Ugandan martyrs.

38.contenido: 38. A subsequent requirement pointed out by the Cardinals and Bishops is that of Synods of a continental nature, along the lines of those already held for Europe and Africa. The last General Conference of the Latin American Episcopate has welcomed, in harmony with the North American Episcopate, the proposal of a Pan-American Synod on the problem of the new evangelization in the two parts of the same continent, so diverse from each other due to their origin and history, and on the question of justice and international economic relations, considering the enormous inequality between the North and the South.

39.contenido: 39. On the basis of this extensive awareness-raising action it will then be possible to undertake the second phase, the actual preparatory phase. This will take place over a period of three years, from 1997 to 1999. The ideal structure for this triennium, centered on Christ, the Son of God made man, must be theological, that is, "Trinitarian."

40.contenido: 40. The first year, 1997, will be dedicated to reflection on Christ, Word of the Father, made man by the work of the Holy Spirit. It is necessary to highlight the clearly Christological character of the Jubilee, which will celebrate the Incarnation and the coming into the world of the Son of God, a mystery of salvation for the entire human race. The general theme, proposed for this year by many Cardinals and Bishops, is: "Jesus Christ, only Savior of the world, yesterday, today and forever" ( [+[0]+] ).

41.contenido: 41. The effort at sacramental updating mentioned above can help, throughout the year, to discover Baptism as the foundation of Christian existence, according to the Apostle's word: "All of you who are baptized into Christ have put on Christ" ([+[0]+]). The Catechism of the Catholic Church, for its part, recalls that Baptism constitutes "the foundation of communion among all Christians, and even with those who are not yet in full communion with the Catholic Church." Under the ecumenical profile, it will be a very important year to look together at Christ, the only Lord, with the intention of becoming one thing in Him, according to his prayer to the Father. The accentuation of the centrality of Christ, of the Word of God and of faith should not fail to arouse interest and favorable reception among Christians of other Confessions.

42.contenido: 42. Everything must look at the priority objective of the Jubilee, which is the strengthening of the faith and testimony of Christians. It is necessary to arouse in each faithful a true desire for holiness, a strong desire for conversion and personal renewal in a climate of ever more intense prayer and solidarity with others, especially those most in need.

43.contenido: 43. Most Holy Mary, who will be present in a so to speak "transverse" way throughout the entire preparatory phase, will be contemplated during this first year in the mystery of her divine Motherhood. In her womb the Word became flesh! The affirmation of the centrality of Christ cannot be, therefore, separated from the recognition of the role played by his Blessed Mother. Their worship, although valuable, should in no way undermine "the dignity and effectiveness of Christ, the only Mediator." Mary, constantly dedicated to her Divine Son, is proposed to all Christians as a model of lived faith. "The Church, meditating on her with love and contemplating her in the light of the Word made man, full of veneration, penetrates more intimately into the supreme mystery of the Incarnation and identifies herself more and more with her Spouse."

44.contenido: 44. 1998, the second year of the preparatory phase, will be dedicated in a particular way to the Holy Spirit and his sanctifying presence within the community of Christ's disciples. «The great Jubilee, which will conclude the second millennium – he wrote in the Encyclical Dominum et vivificantem – ( [+[0]+] ) has a pnemautological dimension, since the mystery of the Incarnation was carried out by the work of the Holy Spirit. It was accomplished by that Spirit who "consubstantial with the Father and the Son" is, in the absolute mystery of the one and triune God, the Person-love, the uncreated gift, eternal source of all life that comes from God in the order of creation, the direct principle and, in a certain way, the subject of God's self-communication in the order of grace. "The mystery of the Incarnation constitutes the culmination of this gift and this divine self-communication."

45.contenido: 45. Therefore, among the primary objectives of the preparation for the Jubilee is the recognition of the presence and action of the Spirit, who acts in the Church both sacramentally, especially through Confirmation, and through the various charismas, tasks and ministries that He has raised for her good: "It is the same Spirit who, according to his richness and the needs of the ministries ([+[0]+]), distributes his various gifts for the good of the Church. Among these gifts, the grace of the Apostles stands out, to whose authority the Spirit himself subjects even the charismatics ( [+[1]+] ). The Spirit himself personally, with his strength and with the intimate connection of the members, gives unity to the body and thus produces and stimulates love among believers.

46.contenido: 46. In this eschatological dimension, believers will be called to rediscover the theological virtue of hope, about which "you were already instructed by the Word of truth, the Gospel" ([+[0]+]). The fundamental attitude of hope, on the one hand, moves the Christian not to lose sight of the final goal that gives meaning and value to his entire existence and, on the other hand, it offers him solid and deep motivations for the daily effort to transform reality to make it conform to God's project.

47.contenido: 47. The reflection of the faithful in the second year of preparation should focus with particular concern on the value of unity within the Church, towards which the different gifts and charismas raised in her by the Spirit tend. For this purpose, it will be possible to delve further into the ecclesiological doctrine of the Second Vatican Council, contained above all in the dogmatic Constitution Lumen gentium. This important document has expressly emphasized that the unity of the Body of Christ is founded on the action of the Holy Spirit, is guaranteed by the apostolic ministry and sustained by reciprocal love ( [+[0]+] ). Such catechetical deepening of the faith will lead the members of the People of God to a more mature awareness of their own responsibilities, as well as a more vivid sense of the value of ecclesial obedience.

48.contenido: 48. Mary, who conceived the incarnate Word through the work of the Holy Spirit and then allowed herself to be guided throughout her entire existence by his interior action, will be contemplated and imitated throughout this year above all as the woman docile to the voice of the Spirit, a woman of silence and listening, a woman of hope, who knew how to accept, like Abraham, the will of God "hoping against all hope" ([+[0]+]). She has brought to its full expression the longing of the poor of Yhaveh, and shines as a model for those who trust with all their hearts in the promises of God.

49.contenido: 49. 1999, the third and final preparatory year, will have the function of expanding the horizons of the believer according to the very vision of Christ: the vision of the "Heavenly Father" ([+[0]+]), by whom he was sent and to whom he will return ([+[1]+]).

50.contenido: 50. In this third year the meaning of the "path to the Father" must lead everyone to undertake, in adhesion to Christ the Redeemer of man, a path of authentic conversion, which includes both a "negative" aspect of liberation from sin, and a "positive" aspect of choosing the good, manifested by the ethical values contained in the natural law, confirmed and deepened by the Gospel. This is the appropriate context for the rediscovery and intense celebration of the sacrament of Penance in its deepest meaning. The announcement of conversion as an essential requirement of Christian love is particularly important in today's society, where the very foundations of an ethical vision of human existence often seem to fade.

51.contenido: 51. In this sense, remembering that Jesus came to "evangelize the poor" ([+[0]+]), how can we not emphasize more decisively the Church's preferential option for the poor and the marginalized? It must be said above all that the commitment to justice and peace in a world like ours, marked by so many conflicts and intolerable social and economic inequalities, is an outstanding aspect of the preparation and celebration of the Jubilee. Thus, in the spirit of the Book of Leviticus ( [+[1]+] ), Christians must speak for all the poor in the world, proposing the Jubilee as an opportune time to think, among other things, about a notable reduction, if not a total forgiveness, of the international debt, which burdens the destiny of many nations. The Jubilee may also offer the opportunity to meditate on other challenges of the moment, such as, for example, the difficulty of dialogue between diverse cultures and the problems related to respect for women's rights and the promotion of family and marriage.

52.contenido: 52. Remembering, furthermore, that "Christ ([+[0]+]) in the same revelation of the mystery of the Father and his love, fully manifests man to himself and reveals to him the sublimity of his vocation", two commitments will be unavoidable especially during the third preparatory year: the confrontation with secularism and the dialogue with the great religions.

53.contenido: 53. At the same time, regarding the horizon of religious consciousness, the 2000 eve will be a great occasion, also in light of the events of recent decades, for interreligious dialogue, according to the clear indications given by the Second Vatican Council in the Declaration Nostra Aetate on the relations of the Church with non-Christian religions.

54.contenido: 54. In this extensive program, the Most Holy Mary, favorite daughter of the Father, is presented to the eyes of believers as a perfect example of love, both for God and neighbor. As she herself affirms in the canticle of the Magnificat, great things have been done in her by the Almighty, whose name is Holy ([+[0]+]). The Father has chosen Mary for a unique mission in the history of salvation: to be Mother of the Savior himself. The Virgin responded to God's call with full availability: "Behold, the handmaid of the Lord" ([+[1]+]). Her motherhood, begun in Nazareth and lived fully in Jerusalem next to the Cross, will be felt this year as an affectionate and insistent invitation to all the children of God, to return to the Father's house listening to her maternal voice: "Do whatever Christ says" ([+[2]+]).

55.contenido: 55. A particular chapter is the celebration of the Great Jubilee itself, which will take place simultaneously in the Holy Land, in Rome and in the local Churches throughout the world. Above all in this phase, the celebratory phase, the objective will be the glorification of the Trinity, from which everything comes and to which everything is directed, in the world and in history. The three years of immediate preparation look at this mystery: from Christ and through Christ, in the Holy Spirit, to the Father. In this sense, the jubilee celebration updates and at the same time anticipates the goal and fulfillment of the life of the Christian and the Church in the triune God.

56.contenido: 56. The Church has endured for 2000 years. Like the evangelical mustard seed, it grows until it becomes a great tree, capable of covering all of humanity with its branches ([+[0]+]). The Second Vatican Council in the Dogmatic Constitution on the Church, considering the question of belonging to the Church and of ordination to the People of God, says: "All men are invited to this Catholic unity of the People of God ([+[1]+]). Catholics, other Christians and even all men in general called to salvation by the grace of God belong to this unity in various ways or are destined to it. Paul VI, for his part, in the Encyclical Ecclesiam suam explains the universal participation of men in God's project, pointing out the different circles of the dialogue of salvation.

57.contenido: 57. For this reason, since apostolic times, the mission of the Church within the universal human family has continued without interruption. The first evangelization dealt especially with the region of the Mediterranean Sea. Throughout the first millennium, missionaries, leaving from Rome and Constantinople, brought Christianity to the interior of the European continent. At the same time they headed towards the heart of Asia, to India and China. The end of the 15th century, together with the discovery of America, marked the beginning of evangelization in this great continent, in the south and in the north. At the same time, while the South Saharan coasts of Africa welcomed the light of Christ, Saint Francis Xavier, patron of the missions, arrived in Japan. Between the 18th and 19th centuries, a layman, Andrew Kim, brought Christianity to Korea; At that time the evangelical announcement reached the Indochinese Peninsula, as well as Australia and the Pacific islands.

58.contenido: 58. The future of the world and the Church belongs to the young generations who, born in this century, will be mature in the next, the first of the new millennium. Christ listens to young people, as he listened to the young man who asked him the question: "What good must I do to obtain eternal life?" » ( [+[0]+] ). I have made reference to the magnificent answer that Jesus gave him in the recent Encyclical Veritatis splendor, as, previously, in the "Letter to the young men and women of the world" of 1985. Young people, in every situation, in every region of the earth do not stop asking Christ: they find him and seek him to question him next. If you know how to follow the path that He indicates, you will have the joy of making your own contribution to your presence in the next century and in the following centuries, until the consummation of time. «Jesus is the same yesterday, today and forever».

59.contenido: 59. To conclude, the words of the Pastoral Constitution Gaudium et Spes are appropriate: “The Church believes that Christ, who died and rose for all, gives man light and strength through his Spirit, so that he can respond to his highest vocation; and that no other name has been given to men under heaven by which they must be saved. Likewise, he believes that the key, the center and the end of all human history is found in his Lord and Master. The Church further affirms that, in all changes, many things remain that do not change and that have their ultimate foundation in Christ, who is the same yesterday, today and forever. Therefore, in the light of Christ, Image of the invisible God, Firstborn of every creature, the Council intends to speak to everyone to illuminate the mystery of man and to cooperate in the discovery of the solution to the main problems of our time.
